prompts.prompt:
Use case: lighting-weather / precise-object-edit. Make ONE full-frame game art proposal by editing image 1, the actual intoDeDung tactical battle screenshot. Image 2 is supporting identity reference for the allied Defender only. Preserve the screenshot's exact whole-scene composition and 4:3 isometric tile projection, same board footprint, framing, tile grid, camera, dark navy background, Russian UI and all UI positions, traps, cube obstacle, raised tiles, fire, slime, soldier placements and placeholder cyan characters. Do not crop any part of the screenshot. No new scenery, architecture, foliage mass, props, UI, badges, headings or labels. Do not redesign the Defender: keep the silver helmet and broad shoulders, olive shield and tabard, brown leather, short sword, same pose and original pixel-art silhouette. Reduce the allied Defender at upper left AND the two grey enemy Defenders on the right to 80 percent of their respective original linear sprite dimensions. Scale each about the midpoint between its grounded boots, keeping the feet at the same ground point and retaining faction facing. Shorten their ground shadows appropriately, place existing little health bars adjacent to their smaller feet without enlarging those bars. Other classes retain size. Style must remain quiet readable game pixel art with deliberate crisp pixel clusters, flat material color planes and limited shades, NOT painterly or smooth 3D. Keep grass sparse and existing tile textures calm. Do not alter terrain geometry or obscure tactical readability. Need visible local depth from grounded shadows, darker side faces, clear light versus shade planes on grass clumps, cool armor sides with restrained highlights. Shadows must stay transparent enough to see tile boundaries. This is an art mockup, no game implementation.
Variant A: restrained daytime tonal depth. Keep the existing muted olive/earth palette but lower the terrain midtones about 15 percent perceptually; subtly cooler green shaded regions. Make darkest occlusion under boots, grass roots, wall base and raised tiles considerably deeper and coherent, with short soft-edged PIXEL-CLUSTER shadows away from upper-left daylight. Emphasize raised tile side faces and wall faces, not thick grid outlines. Keep armor silver with smaller highlight areas instead of broad white glows. Broad ground surfaces stay calm and legible; daylight stays clear, no dramatic spotlight or global black filter. This should feel like the same scene, more solid and less washed out.
